references.text: Matthew's parallel account of the wise and foolish builders. Jesus uses the same parable about those who hear his words and do them, compared to those who hear but do not act.
James urges believers to be doers of the word and not merely hearers—the same principle of not just listening to God's word but acting on it.
Jesus says that not everyone who says 'Lord, Lord' will enter the kingdom of heaven, but only those who do the will of his heavenly Father—emphasizing the importance of doing, not just hearing.
Jesus states that his disciples are blessed if they do what they know—linking knowledge and action, as in Luke 6:47.
Paul emphasizes that it is not the hearers of the law who are righteous before God, but the doers of the law—the same theme that action, not merely hearing, is decisive.
Moses says that blessings follow if the people listen to the Lord's voice and keep his commandments—an Old Testament background for the principle of hearing and doing.
Joshua is urged to meditate on the Book of the Law and do everything written in it—both listening/reading and acting are necessary for progress.
Ezekiel describes the people as those who hear God's word but do not act on it—a warning that highlights the contrast Jesus draws between hearing and doing.
Jesus says: 'Blessed are those who hear God's word and keep it'—the same connection between hearing and obeying God's word.
Jesus defines his family as those who hear God's word and do it—confirming the principle from Luke 6:47 about coming to him, listening, and acting.
